## Engineering standards
- Workflow: understand -> smallest correct change -> run `bash scripts/verify.sh` -> summarize the diff. One concern per commit, Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, chore:, docs:, refactor:).
- Code: typed where possible, no dead code, no copy-paste, errors handled; every data view has loading, empty and error states; no secrets or demo credentials in code.
- Security: validate and sanitize server-side, parameterized queries only, RLS on every exposed Supabase table, service-role key server-only, hashed passwords, rate-limit auth by account and IP, expiring/revocable sessions, security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy), no default passwords in production seeds.
- Web UX: mobile-first, responsive, semantic HTML, WCAG 2.1 AA (labels, contrast, keyboard, focus, alt text), Core Web Vitals (sized images, lazy loading, minimal JS), SEO basics (title, meta, Open Graph, sitemap, robots), custom 404/500 pages, working /api/health that checks the database.
- Data: migrations are numbered SQL files, schema separate from seed data, nothing destructive without an explicit backup/rollback note.
- Docs: README covers setup, env var NAMES, deploy steps and rollback. Record notable changes in CHANGELOG.
- Definition of done: verify passes, no new warnings, no secrets in diff, docs updated, checked at a 360px mobile viewport.
- Commands: /scope (audit scope), /verify (quality gate), /secure (security review), /ship (pre-deploy checklist).
